{{Short description|American physicist and professor}}
'''George H. Rawitscher''' (27 February 1928 – 10 March 2018)<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.legacy.com/obituaries/name/george-rawitscher-obituary?pid=188450435&view=guestbook|title=George Rawitscher Obituary - Death Notice and Service Information|website=[[Legacy.com]]|date=14 March 2018}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.tributes.com/obituary/show/George-Heinrich-Rawitscher-105919352 |title=George Rawitscher Obituary - Connecticut |publisher=Tributes.com |date= |accessdate=2022-10-09}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=https://physics.uconn.edu/2018/03/20/in-memoriam-george-h-rawitscher-1928-2018/ |title=In memoriam – George H. Rawitscher (1928-2018) |publisher=physics.uconn.edu |accessdate=March 20, 2018}}</ref> was an American [[physicist]] who taught at the [[University of Connecticut]].

Rawitscher in his research focused on scattering problems which involve non-local [[optical]] models, reaction mechanisms involving break-up and virtual [[nuclear excitation]]s, the (e,e’p) reaction. He also worked on numerical methods such as [[Galerkin method]] and [[spectral expansion]]s for solving [[integral equations]]

Rawitcher was an Elected Fellow of the [[American Physical Society]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.aps.org/programs/honors/fellowships/archive-all.cfm |title=Fellows |publisher=aps.org |accessdate=April 24, 2017}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=http://physics.uconn.edu/george-rawitscher/ |title=George Rawitscher |publisher=uconn.edu |accessdate=April 24, 2017}}</ref>
